clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old Indian female presented with uncontrolled hypertension, asymmetric blood pressure (higher in right arm) and diminished pulse in left radial artery, plus exertional angina class 2. Initial labs showed elevated ESR and CRP inflammatory markers. MR angiography demonstrated complete thrombosis of the left subclavian and left common carotid arteries and 80-90% luminal narrowing of thoracic and abdominal aorta. Coronary angiography revealed diffuse coronary artery stenoses and a porcelain aorta. Peripheral angiography showed multiple stenoses in right subclavian and bilateral renal arteries, with non-visualization of left subclavian artery. No autoimmune panel results were reported. This constellation of clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings supports the diagnosis of Takayasu vasculitis.
